name: Delaware
headline_status: Recreational and medical cannabis are legal for adults 21+; adult-use stores opened August 1, 2025.
summary: Delaware legalized adult-use cannabis in April 2023 when Gov. John Carney let HB 1 and HB 2 become law without his signature, and licensed adult-use sales began August 1, 2025. Adults 21+ may possess up to one ounce of flower, 12 grams of concentrate or 750 mg of THC in products, but home cultivation is not allowed. Adult purchases carry a 15% tax, while medical patients, served under a program dating to 2011, buy tax-free.

adult_use_since.value: HB 1 (possession) and HB 2 (regulated sales) became law without the governor's signature in April 2023; the Delaware Marijuana Control Act took effect July 5, 2023.

medical_since.value: The General Assembly created the medical marijuana program in 2011.

possession_limit.value: Personal-use quantity: up to 1 ounce of flower, up to 12 grams of concentrate, or products containing up to 750 mg of delta-9 THC.

home_grow.value: Not allowed; the law does not permit home cultivation.

purchase_age.value: 21 and older, except registered medical patients.

public_use.value: Consuming in areas open to the public or in a vehicle is illegal; public use draws a civil citation with a fine and possible short jail time.

retail_sales.value: Adult-use sales began Aug. 1, 2025, initially at existing medical dispensaries (compassion centers) holding conversion licenses.

taxes.value: 15% tax on adult-use purchases; medical purchases are tax-exempt.

medical_program.value: Clinicians may recommend cannabis for any diagnosed condition they believe it could help (HB 285); patients 65+ can self-certify, and out-of-state cards are recognized. Patients may buy 3 ounces every 14 days, up to 6 ounces a month.

regulator.value: Office of the Marijuana Commissioner (OMC), which now oversees both adult-use and medical programs.

dui.value: Zero tolerance: Delaware is among the states that ban driving with any amount of THC or its metabolites in the body.

tourists.value: Yes. Adults 21+ may buy up to the personal-use quantity (1 ounce of flower, 12 grams of concentrate or 750 mg of THC in products). Out-of-state medical patients can register at a dispensary for a visiting-patient card; products may not leave Delaware.

faq.a: Yes. Adults 21 and older can possess cannabis, and licensed stores have sold to adults since Aug. 1, 2025.

faq.q: How much weed can you buy or carry in Delaware?
faq.a: Up to one ounce of flower, 12 grams of concentrate, or products with up to 750 mg of THC.

faq.q: Can you grow weed at home in Delaware?
faq.a: No. Delaware's law does not allow home cultivation, even for adults 21+.

faq.q: What is the tax on recreational weed in Delaware?
faq.a: Adult-use purchases are taxed at 15%. Registered medical patients pay no tax.

faq.q: Can you smoke weed in public in Delaware?
faq.a: No. Using cannabis in public or in a vehicle is illegal and can lead to a civil citation with a fine and possible short jail time.
